acceptance: Exports and config keys with no caller or enforcing reader are removed, each named in a breaking-change changelog entry.
A config file that still sets a removed key gets a message pointing to `execution.timeout_seconds`.
Plan capture is bounded by the run deadline, and product code has one process-group kill helper.
description:
## Problem
Timers that nothing uses, and settings that promise a limit and enforce nothing. Read on develop: `benchbox/utils/timeout_manager.py` exports `TimeoutManager`, `get_timeout_manager`, `timeout`, `TimeoutConfig` and `TimeoutError` (utils/__init__.py:34-41,65-70) with no caller outside their own tests; `run_with_timeout` is used only by plan capture (platforms/base/result_capture.py:51,657,707) and abandons a running thread. `ResourceLimitsConfig.default_operation_timeout` and `enforce_timeouts` are read only by `from_config_dict` (utils/resource_limits.py:91-92) and tests. Config keys with no enforcing reader: `benchmarks.timeout_minutes` (60), `execution.power_run.timeout_per_iteration_minutes` (60; 120 and 45 in presets; cli/config.py:41,239,326,329; utils/config_helpers.py:23,143-145,264), `execution.concurrent_queries.query_timeout_seconds` (300; config_helpers.py:52,63,151-153,171-222,306). Process-group kill code is duplicated: utils/resource_limits.py, utils/host_lock.py:1049-1068,1169, utils/linux_machine.py:339, core/tpcds/qualification/runner.py:728-731, scripts/run_version_matrix.py, scripts/remote_review.py, scripts/release_artifact_consumer.py:921 (utils/heavy_watchdog.py signals one pid at a time and is not a group helper).

## Owner decisions
Timers: "remove the ones with no caller, move plan capture onto the new deadline, and record the removal in the changelog as a breaking change to `benchbox.utils`." Config keys: "in step 5, re-verify that nothing enforces them, then remove all three and say so in the breaking-change changelog entry. A config file that still sets one gets a clear message pointing to `execution.timeout_seconds`." No new CI check. Source: owner's answer in the choice dialog, 2026-11-20.

## Change
1. Re-verify each name and key on current develop. A caller means product code, scripts, docs or examples; a name's own tests do not count and are deleted with it. Use the language server's references and list the evidence.
2. Remove the five unused `timeout_manager` exports, the two `ResourceLimitsConfig` fields with their `from_config_dict` keys, and the three config keys with their presets and helpers. A config file that sets a removed key gets a message naming `execution.timeout_seconds`.
3. Plan capture keeps its own `plan_capture_timeout_seconds` setting and value, bounded by min(setting, time remaining).
4. Product code under `benchbox/` uses the one process-group helper step 1b put in `benchbox/utils`; delete the duplicates there. Scripts that do not import `benchbox` keep theirs.

## Decision gates
A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). The removed-key message is the owner's text verbatim (2026-11-21): "`{key}` is no longer used and has no effect. Use `execution.timeout_seconds` to limit a run." A name or key with a real caller or enforcing reader is not removed; report it. The heavy watchdog's and the host lock's kill behaviour (signals, order, waits) must not change: if the shared helper differs from what they do today, leave them and say so. Plan capture keeps its own 30-second default (owner, 2026-11-21: it bounds an optional diagnostic, not the run); do not change it.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the references evidence per removed name and key is in the pull request; `import benchbox.utils` works and the removed names are absent (test); loading a config file that sets each removed key produces the message (test per key) and does not crash; plan-capture tests cover min(setting, remaining); heavy-watchdog and host-lock tests pass unchanged; `make duplicate-check-delta` reports no new duplicate helper; the changelog entry is marked breaking and names each removed export and key (checked against the diff); `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking; `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job that never ran or was cancelled by the runner, never for a test that failed. Review threads: reply, and resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again. Subagents implement batch members and serial items under the delivery plan on run-timeout-plan-20261120 (owner, 2026-11-21); a batch member makes no tracker write, opens no pull request and stops at a landing report. A limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has chosen is used verbatim (see run-timeout-plan-20261120). Any other new name or message follows existing BenchBox conventions and is listed in the pull request (owner, 2026-11-21: no stop for these). No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment. A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`.
